name: Nerio Alessandri
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2021-2025); Hurun Global (2024-2026)
forbes_bio: Nerio Alessandri is the founder and president of the Italian gym and fitness equipment manufacturer Technogym.
Alessandri founded the company in Cesena, Italy in 1983 at age 22.
Alessandri took the company public on the Milan Stock Exchange in 2016.
When he started Technogym, Alessandri designed and built the first pieces of equipment in his garage.
Technogym has been the official supplier at eight Olympic Games, from Sydney 2000 to Tokyo 2020.
forbes_facts: Alessandri has written several books on the concept of wellness, with his latest book "Born to Move" published in 2014.

name: Chen Qixing
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2017-2025); Hurun Global (2017-2026); Hurun China (2010-2026)
forbes_bio: Chen Qixing is the chairman of Shenzhen Everwin Precision Technology, a Shenzhen-listed electronics component manufacturer.
Chen was a government official in Anhui Province before becoming an entrepreneur.

name: Ronnie Screwvala
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2025); Hurun Global (2022-2026); Hurun Unicorn founders (2021-2026)
forbes_bio: Ronnie Screwvala is the cofounder and chairperson of Mumbai-based edtech firm upGrad.
He set up the firm in 2015 after a successful career in the media business as the founder of the UTV group.
He sold his stake in UTV to the Walt Disney Company for over $450 million in 2012 and ran the India unit as managing director. He stepped down two years later.
Screwvala has other investments in startups such as eyewear firm Lenskart and also owns sports franchises.
Along with wife Zarina, he founded nonprofit Swades Foundation, which focuses on rural upliftment projects.

name: Bill Liu
forbes_bio: Bill Liu, also known as Liu Zihong, is the chairman and CEO of Roylole Corp., a supplier of flexible screens.
He owns about 40% of Roylole, which has an office near Silicon Valley in Fremont, California.
Liu holds a doctorate from Stanford University and worked for IBM after graduation.

name: Djoko Susanto
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2012-2025); Hurun Global (2014-2026)
forbes_bio: Djoko Susanto is the founder of Alfamart, which has more than 22,000 convenience stores across Indonesia and 2,000 stores in the Philippines.
The sixth of 10 siblings, he started managing his parents' modest food stall inside a traditional market in Jakarta at age 17.
He later partnered with clove cigarette tycoon Putera Sampoerna to open similar stalls and then a discount supermarket chain.
When Putera sold his cigarette business to Philip Morris in 2005, Susanto bought the retail business and developed it into the Alfamart chain.
In 2022, the company bought a $30 million stake in Bank Aladin Syariah, which provides sharia-compliant financial services.
forbes_facts: Susanto's daughter Feny and sons, Budiyanto and Harryanto, hold senior positions at Alfamart.
His property division Alfaland operates Omega Hotel Management throughout Indonesia.
His Bunda Mulia University in Jakarta, founded in 2003, offers programs in everything from digital business to visual communication to informatics.

name: John Coustas
forbes_bio: John Coustas is the chairman and CEO of Athens, Greece-based shipping firm Danaos Corporation.
His father Dimitris Coustas (d. 2013) founded the company in 1972.
John Coustas succeeded his father as CEO in 1987 and took Danaos public on the New York Stock Exchange in 2006.
He owns just over 50% of the company's stock.
He also serves as deputy chairman of the board of international marine insurance company The Swedish Club.

name: Lu Ruibo
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2026); Hurun China (2019-2026); Hurun Global (2026)
forbes_bio: Lu Ruibo is the founder and chairman of Impro Precision Industries, a manufacturer of casting and machined components.
Customers of the company include Bosch, Caterpillar, Cummins, Honeywell, HUSCO and Parker Hannifin.
The company has over 7,000 employees.

name: Georg Haub
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes annual (2019-2025); Hurun Global (2019-2026)
forbes_bio: Georg Haub derives his fortune from Tengelmann Group, which began with a shop opened in Muelheim an der Ruhr in 1876. Georg holds 31.33% of the group.
Its operations include home-improvement chain OBI; clothing and non-food discounter KiK; online retailer babymarkt.de; and food production company No Meat Factor.
The group also invests in startups and is active in services (energy, plus audits and consulting), property management and real estate development.
Oldest brother Karl-Erivan and Christian had taken over as co-CEOs in 2000. In 2018, Karl-Erivan went missing while on a ski tour. In 2021, he was declared dead.
With Karl-Erivan presumed dead, Georg's younger brother, Christian, who had been overseeing Tengelmann's U.S. venture portfolio, took over as CEO.
forbes_facts: Erivan Haub had strong ties to Tacoma, WA, where his sons were born. He was a major contributor to UW-Tacoma, the Museum of Glass and the LeMay Automobile Museum

name: Kim Hyoung-nyon
forbes_bio: Kim Hyoung-nyon is cofounder and vice chairman of Dunamu, which operates Upbit, South Korea's largest crypto exchange by daily trading volume.
In November 2025, South Korean search engine behemoth Naver said its payment arm, Naver Financial, will acquire Dunamu in a stock swap that values the combined entity at $13.6 billion.
Dunamu's previous investors include Kakao Ventures, Silicon Valley-based venture capital firm Altos Ventures and Hybe, the agency behind K-pop powerhouse BTS.
Before starting Dunamu with Song Chi-hyung, who is also a billionaire, Kim worked at local mobile payment company Danal.

name: Ajlan bin Abdulaziz Al-Ajlan
forbes_bio: Ajlan bin Abdulaziz Al-Ajlan is the chairman of Ajlan & Bros Group, a large Saudi conglomerate with investments in textiles, real estate, mining, energy, logistics, technology and tourism.
He founded Ajlan & Bros in 1979 as a shop specializing in fabric and garments, going on to open a factory in China in 1990 and move into real estate in the 2000s.
The company has operations in more than 25 countries on four continents, including the U.S. and China.
In 2000, Al-Ajlan launched Abdulaziz Alajlan Sons for Trading & Real Estate Investments, which owns residential projects in Saudi Arabia and more than 20,000 residential units under construction.
Al-Ajlan is also a member of the Saudi Shura Council, a 150-member body.

name: Lívia Voigt de Assis
appears_on: Forbes real-time (2026); Forbes real-time (former) (2025); Forbes annual (2024-2025); Hurun Global (2025-2026); Wikidata (2024)
forbes_bio: Lívia Voigt de Assis, one of the world's youngest billionaires, is one of the largest individual shareholders of WEG, the largest manufacturer of electrical motors in Latin America.
At twenty years old, she is the world's second-youngest billionaire, behind nineteen-year-old German pharmaceuticals heir Johannes von Baumbach.
WEG was cofounded by her grandfather Werner Ricardo Voigt along with late billionaires Eggon Joao da Silva and Geraldo Werninghaus.
A publicly-traded multinational with factories in over ten countries, WEG has annual revenue of approximately $7 billion.
Lívia does not hold a board seat or any executive position at WEG; she is currently attending university.
forbes_facts: Voigt de Assis was the world's youngest billionaire in 2025 before losing the spot to German pharmaceutical heir, Johannes von Baumbach, a year later.

name: Peyush Bansal
forbes_bio: Peyush Bansal founded Lenskart Solutions a retailer of eyewear in 2010 together with his sister Neha and two others.
Lenskart has a presence in 157 cities across India and 15 other countries.
The company is backed by Japan's SoftBank Group and has a slew of marquee investors including Abu Dhabi Investment Authority, KKR and TPG.
Lenskart was listed in November 2025 and raised $821 million in its IPO.
Neha is an executive director on the board and the global head of merchandising,
forbes_facts: Bansal has an undergrad degree in electrical engineering from Canada's McGill University.

name: Yvon Chouinard
appears_on: Forbes real-time (former) (2022); Forbes annual (2017-2022); Hurun Global (2018-2022)
forbes_bio: Yvon Chouinard is founder of outdoor wear maker Patagonia, based in Ventura, California.
Since Patagonia was founded in 1984, it has has an open office plan - not even Chouinard, the owner, has his own office.
His apparel business took off in the 1970s when Chouinard imported rugby shirts from England and sold them to climbers.
Since 1985, Patagonia has set aside 1% of sales to finance grassroots environmental groups in the U.S. and abroad. Revenues hit $800 million in 2017.
In May 2013 Patagonia launched Tin Shed Ventures which provides seed funding to environmentally and socially responsible start-ups.
forbes_facts: On Black Friday 2011, Patagonia ran a full-page ad in The New York Times encouraging customers not to buy its products, but to reuse or repair items instead.
An avid climber, Chouinard taught himself blacksmithing in 1957 to make reusable climbing tools that wouldn't pollute the environment.
